text: My American Dream began when my family immigrated from Saigon in search of freedom. The adjustment wasn’t easy, but through hard work, I became the first in my family to graduate from college.
In 2012, I was honored to become the first Vietnamese-American elected mayor. As Mayor, I focused on the basics—public safety, fixing roads, and improving quality of life—and delivered real results.
Four years ago, I ran for Assembly to help more families achieve a middle-class life, prioritize public safety, and give back to the country that gave me so much.

As your Assemblyman, I have passed legislation to strengthen public safety and push back against pro-criminal policies coming out of Sacramento. When insurance companies wrongly denied care to autistic children, I authored tough legislation and overcame a Governor’s veto to protect families.

I have consistently stood up for taxpayers and opposed tax increases. California is already the highest-taxed state, and family budgets are stretched thin. I also authored legislation to rein in rising utility costs, fought corruption, and secured $1 million in new park funding for our district.
I have lived in this district for over 20 years, and my wife and I are proud to have raised our daughters here.

I am honored to be endorsed by the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association Pac, California Association of Highway Patrolmen, California Professional Firefighters, and California Women’s Leadership Association.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: I’m Dr. Paula Swift, and I’m running for Assembly because Orange County families deserve a representative who understands what it means to stretch a paycheck, navigate a broken healthcare system, and worry about whether the next generation can afford to stay in the community they grew up in.
I know what resources our communities need, and I know what is at stake when Sacramento gets it wrong.

I put myself through school while raising my family. I earned my bachelor's degree from Azusa Pacific University and a Master’s and Doctorate in Leadership from the University of Southern California. After surviving a tragic act of domestic violence, I've dedicated my work to protecting those overlooked by a government meant to protect them.

Today I own a small business, have taught at a local college, and spent over two decades serving Southern California families, supporting children in foster care and fighting to improve access to mental health care and educational opportunities.

As your Assemblymember, I will fight to make healthcare more accessible and affordable. I will push for housing solutions that offer pathways to homeownership. I will work to expand opportunities for our students, protect our seniors’ retirement security, and increase support for the small businesses that give our communities their character.
We need leadership focused on lowering the cost of living and bringing accountability to our State Capitol. I have the life experience to deliver it.
A future shaped by opportunity, not circumstance.
I ask for your vote. Learn more: votepaulaswift.com
